newsitem.title: USA: FBI informant is said to link Jack Kemp to the mob.
newsitem.headline: FBI informant is said to link Jack Kemp to the mob.

text.p: An FBI informant told the staff of a House of Representatives committee that Republican vice presidential nominee Jack Kemp had links to organised crime figures, the committee's top Democrat said on Monday.
Representative John Conyers, a Michigan Democrat, asked the committee's Republican chairman, Rep, Henry Hyde of Illinois, to authorise further questioning of the informant, Ronald Fino.
Kemp spokeswoman Alixe Glenn called the charges referred to by Conyers "unfounded and politically motivated."

Fino testified last July at a House Judiciary Committee hearing on a consent agreement between the Labourers' International Union of North America and the Justice Department, under which the union agreed to rid itself of mob influence.
The hearing focused on whether the White House had improper contacts with union officials accused of having associations with organised crime. Democrats charged the hearing was politically motivated.

In a letter to Hyde, Conyers said Fino "is now alleging that Republican vice president candidate Jack Kemp has knowingly involved himself with organised crime associates and officials within the Labourers International who, prior to the consent agreement, were involved in illegal activities."
An aide to Conyers said Fino presented the "circumstantial evidence" in an interview with committee staff and to the FBI. He said Conyers had not received a reply from Hyde to his Sept. 18 letter.

Conyers said Fino was alleging that Kemp "had claimed to have personal knowledge that certain named individuals were involved with organised crime, that alleged associates of organised crime contributed to (former Housing) Secretary Kemp's political campaigns and that such persons benefited from federal grants and contracts as a result of Secretary Kemp's efforts on their behalf."
Conyers said he was not asking for public hearings on Fino's allegations.

But referring to Republicans' praise for Fino as a witness during the July hearing, Conyers said, "Nevetheless, the fact that such serious allegations are being made by a witness the majority obviously considers so credible ... indicates to me that further inquiry into this matter is required."
